GAMEPAD PARTY / DOCUMENTATION

Engine support

Which engines Gamepad Party supports, how far, and where to start. Pick the row for your engine, then follow its guide. If your engine is not listed as Full, read its open work before you start: you write that part yourself.

Support levels

  • Full: an SDK in this repository handles the connection, lifecycle, per-seat controllers and the game window. Released games use it and CI runs its contract tests.
  • New: an SDK covers everything Full does, but no released game uses it yet. Its open work below says what CI checks and what still needs hardware.
  • Partial: an SDK handles the connection and lifecycle. You wire controllers, windows or faces into your engine yourself.
  • Protocol only: no SDK. Write an adapter against the protocol.
Engine Level Start with Games using it

LÖVE / Lua Full Shared party runner Blast Party, Neon Trails, Neon Siege, Volley Trouble, Stack Together, Bubble Buddies
Bevy New gamenight-bevy plugin and the Star Catch demo Star Catch (demo)
Rust Partial gamenight-sdk crate Terminal demo game
C / C++ Partial sdk/c/gamenight.h None yet (transport example only)
Unity New sdk/unity package and the Orb Rush demo Orb Rush (demo)
Unreal Engine 5 New sdk/unreal plugin and the Dash Derby demo Dash Derby (demo)
Other engines Protocol only Wire protocol Mineclonia (Luanti, game-specific adapter)

Open work

This list doubles as the roadmap for engine support.

  • Unity: the package and the Orb Rush demo are new. CI runs the SDK core and the demo rules against a fake host and gamenight-certify with dotnet, and compiles the Unity layer against reference assemblies, but no Unity build has been tested on hardware yet: window handling, faces on screen and pads. Linux has no window hiding. The Input System code path is not compiled in CI.
  • Unreal: the plugin and the Dash Derby demo are new. CI unit tests the plugin's C++ protocol core and runs gamenight-certify against it headless, but has no Unreal build: the module and the demo are not compiled there, and window handling, audio, the world pause, faces on screen and pads are not tested on hardware yet.
  • C / C++: the header has no controller tokens, controller frames, colours or faces, and no phone screens. Games still have to parse those messages themselves.
  • Bevy: the plugin and the Star Catch demo are new. CI builds them with Bevy and runs the demo through gamenight-certify on Linux with software rendering, but Windows and macOS window behaviour, the Windows foreground helper, audio devices and physical pads are not tested on hardware yet.
  • Rust without an engine: the SDK delivers typed events; input, windows and faces are left to the game.
  • Godot 4: Godot has no package manager, so each game vendors the addon. Run sdk/godot/sync.py and the CI check to keep copies current.

For agents and code generators

Use this page to choose an approach, then read only the guide for that engine. Do not invent an SDK where the table says "You" or "No": implement that part against the protocol reference and the controller rules. Before calling an integration done, run the integration checks.
